questions.question: Residual capacities: an original edge $i\to j$ with capacity $c_{ij}$ and flow $x_{ij}$ has residual $c_{ij}-x_{ij}$ forward and $x_{ij}$ in the reverse direction. An augmenting path traverses the reverse direction $j\to i$ of an original edge $i\to j$, and flow is augmented by $\delta$. What happens to $x_{ij}$?
options: It increases by $\delta$, like on every edge of the path.
It is unchanged; a new edge $j\to i$ carries $\delta$ instead.
It drops to 0, whatever the size of $\delta$ compared with it.
It decreases by $\delta$: part of the flow on $i\to j$ is undone.

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. Its four directions have residual capacities 5, 2, 7 and 4. What is its bottleneck $\delta$?

A feasible flow has value 5. An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. One augmenting path has residual capacities 3, 4 and 3. What is the flow value after augmenting along it by its bottleneck?
In the residual network of a feasible flow, a source-to-sink path $S\to A\to B\to T$ has residual capacities 2 on $S\to A$, 0 on $A\to B$ and 4 on $B\to T$. Is it an augmenting path?
options: No; direction $A\to B$ has residual capacity 0.
Yes; two of its three directions have room left.
Yes, with bottleneck 2 from the positive values.
Yes, since the total residual 6 is positive.

questions.question: An augmenting path uses original edge $i\to j$ forwards, with capacity $c_{ij}=6$ and flow $x_{ij}=1$. The flow is augmented by $\delta=3$. What is the new flow on $i\to j$?

Residual capacities: an original edge $i\to j$ with capacity $c_{ij}$ and flow $x_{ij}$ has residual $c_{ij}-x_{ij}$ forward and $x_{ij}$ in the reverse direction. Which directions may an augmenting path from source to sink use?
options: Only forward directions of edges that are below capacity
Reverse directions only of edges that carry no flow at all
Both forward and reverse directions with positive residual
Any original edge, whether or not its residual is positive

questions.question: A feasible flow satisfies conservation at each vertex other than source and sink. An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. After augmenting along it by its bottleneck, which statement about conservation is correct?
options: It fails along the path and must be restored afterwards.
It still holds at each vertex other than source and sink.
It fails wherever the path uses a reverse direction.
It holds, as only the source's outflow is changed at all.

questions.question: A feasible flow has $x_{SA}=1$ on $S\to A$ (capacity 4), $x_{BA}=2$ on $B\to A$ (capacity 5) and $x_{BT}=0$ on $B\to T$ (capacity 6). The residual path $S\to A\to B\to T$ uses $B\to A$ in reverse. What is its bottleneck $\delta$?

A feasible flow has $x_{BA}=2$ on edge $B\to A$ (capacity 5). An augmenting path traverses $A\to B$, the reverse of $B\to A$, and the flow is augmented by $\delta=2$. What is $x_{BA}$ afterwards, and what are its residuals (forward, reverse)?
options: $x_{BA}=4$, residuals $(1,\,4)$
$x_{BA}=2$, residuals $(3,\,2)$
$x_{BA}=0$, residuals $(5,\,0)$
$x_{BA}=0$, residuals $(3,\,2)$

questions.question: On an augmenting path the residual capacities are 4 on $S\to A$, 2 on $A\to C$ and 5 on $C\to T$. Flow is augmented by the bottleneck. What are the three residual capacities afterwards, in the same order?

A flow network has edges $S\to A$, $A\to T$, $S\to B$, $B\to T$, each of capacity 1, and all flows 0. An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. The path $S\to A\to T$ has bottleneck $\delta=1$. What does this $\delta$ tell us?
options: That the flow value can rise by at most 1 in total.
That 1 is the largest flow value this network allows.
That the edges $S\to B$ and $B\to T$ must stay unused.
Only that this path adds 1; others may add more later.

questions.question: A flow network has edges $S\to A$, $S\to B$, $A\to B$, $A\to T$, $B\to T$, each of capacity 1, with flow 1 on $S\to A$, $A\to B$, $B\to T$ and 0 elsewhere. Every $S$–$T$ route along original edges uses a full edge. After augmenting along an augmenting path, which result is possible?
options: Value 1, as every route uses a full edge
Value 2, with $A\to B$ now carrying 2
Value 2, with flow on $A\to B$ cancelled
Value 3, using all three routes to $T$

questions.question: A feasible flow has $x_{SA}=3$ on $S\to A$ (capacity 6), $x_{BA}=3$ on $B\to A$ (capacity 3), $x_{BT}=0$ on $B\to T$ (capacity 5). The augmenting path $S\to A\to B\to T$ uses $B\to A$ in reverse. After augmenting by its bottleneck, how many of its three directions have residual 0?
A flow network has source $s$, sink $t$ and a feasible flow. Which description characterises exactly the augmenting paths for this flow?
options: An $s$–$t$ path in the original network, every edge below capacity
An $s$–$t$ path in the residual network, every direction positive
Any path from $s$ in the residual network with positive residuals
An $s$–$t$ path in the residual network with positive total residual

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. It traverses one reverse direction, so augmenting by its bottleneck $\delta$ lowers the flow on that original edge by $\delta$. What happens to the source-to-sink flow value?
options: It stays the same, as the $+\delta$ and $-\delta$ steps cancel.
It falls by $\delta$, as some flow is cancelled.
It rises by $2\delta$, counting both kinds of step.
It rises by $\delta$, the same as for a forward-only path.
